items.prompt: For centered training Z and sample covariance C=ZᵀZ/(n-1), how does a singular value s relate to its nonzero covariance eigenvalue?

options.why: The covariance contains a squared singular value.
This follows directly from ZᵀZ=V S²Vᵀ.
That would invert rather than express covariance variance.

options.text: λis independent of the normalization convention
options.why: Changing the denominator changes the eigenvalues.

items.explanation: The square and the sample denominator both matter; axis directions alone do not identify the reported variance.
